newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 17.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-July 17.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - French advertising agencies' gross margin rose 3.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997, according to the July newsletter from the agencies' association ACC (Association des Agences Conseils en Communication). Agencies are expecting growth of four percent this year. (Les Echos)
LILLE - A French court orders a hotel chain to withdraw a publicity brochure which featured a photograph of a man, who is undergoing a divorce from his wife, snapped with another woman.
(Reuter)

PARIS - Print unions and distributor Nouvelles Messageries de la Presse have resolved a conflict which took French national newspapers off the streets several times in the last month. (La Tribune, Les Echos, Le Figaro)

PARIS - Jerome Clement, chairman of French public television channels Arte and La Cinquieme, which are in the process of merging, says French public television cannot continue to develop new projects with declining budgets. (Liberation)

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. - Netscape Communications Corp and Excite Inc say Excite will produce a new navigation service to provide international users with a central Internet guide. The new service will be available in Japan, Germany, France, Britain and Australia from respective Netscape Web sites and from localised Netscape Communicator products. (Reuter)
PARIS - Barclays Development Capital, a unit of Barclays Bank, wants to build up a press operation in France with Editions Taitbout, bought in June, as its centre. (La Tribune)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - French drinks and luxury goods firm LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton unveils a plan for a mega drinks merger with British group Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc. Guinness and GrandMet said they would study the plan. In a first reaction they called the plan "complicated and costly". (Reuter)
PARIS - The head of French car parts manufacturer Valeo, Noel Goutard, says he believes the introduction of a single European currency will have a "profound deflationary effect" on prices.
(Reuter)

PARIS - The National Assembly named a special commission on Wednesday to study the automobile industry's future in France and in Europe. Communist deputy Daniel Paul will head the 45-member commission, which will hold its first meeting on August 27, parliamentary aides said. (Reuter)
PARIS - French food group Danone says it bought 50 percent of one of Brazil's largest biscuit makers, Campineira, taking its stake in the company to 100
percent. (Reuter)

TOKYO - Eisai Co Ltd says 12 European countries had approved its drug for Alzheimer's disease and it expects to receive marketing authorisation from the countries in the near future. The approval was issued by drug authorities in Germany, France, Italy, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Ireland, Portugal and Sweden. (Reuter)

LANCASTER, Pa. - Armstrong World Industries Inc says a U.S. District Court set a September 9 hearing for a preliminary injunction to prevent the closing of the deal announced by Sommer Allibert SA of France and Tarkett of Germany. (Reuter)
